title: `go vet`: what it catches before the tests do

videos.script: The compiler tells you whether your code is Go. It does not tell you whether it does what you meant. That is the gap go vet works in. {{report}} Here is a report that prints a percentage. It compiles, it runs, and the number comes out as garbage, because the format asks for an integer and gets a float. Vet reads the format string and says so, with the line and the column. {{list}} Vet is a set of thirty-five small analyzers. Each one looks for one kind of mistake that is legal and almost always wrong. And each one had to prove it rarely raises a false alarm. {{bugs}} Then seven programs that pass the compiler. A mutex copied by value. A context that is never cancelled. A struct tag with one stray space. You will see what each bug does when it runs, and what vet says before it does. {{test}} Next, the vet you already run without asking. go test runs twelve of the analyzers before any test, and a test run can fail on them. Switching that off hid a real bug here, behind a green line. {{limits}} Last, how to choose the checks, how to teach vet about your own logging helper, and what vet will never tell you. That is where lesson 8 begins.
